_comment_file: Shipped defaults for oidc-auth-server (#15). Lowest layer of three: this file, then the host's app-custom-config.json, then the environment for keys listed in oidc-auth-server.config.env-keys. Maps merge per entry; every other value is replaced whole. Settings only: secrets never live in a config file, and callbacks (findAccount, interactionUrl, adapter) are code options passed to createAuthServer.
_comment_issuer: The issuer identifier: https, no query or fragment, including the mount path if any. The host sets it in app-custom-config.json; the empty value here refuses the boot until it is set.
_comment_development: Allows an http issuer and the in-memory adapter. Never true in production.
_comment_acr_values: The acr values the host's sign-in can produce, advertised in discovery. Empty means the host reports none.
_comment_scope_claims: Claims released per scope, beyond openid (which always carries sub, acr, amr and auth_time). Defaults are the four OIDC Core 5.4 scopes: profile, email, address and phone. A map: a host adds a scope without restating these.
_comment_clients: Statically registered clients, as node-oidc-provider client metadata.
_comment_client_id_metadata_document: OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (draft-02): a client, typically an MCP client, identifies itself with an https URL the server fetches. Off unless enabled. allowed-hosts limits which hosts may be fetched; empty means any public host. Fetches never reach private, loopback or link-local addresses, never follow redirects, and stop at 2.5 seconds and 5 KB; if that protection cannot be set up, no fetch happens at all.
_comment_device_flow: OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (RFC 8628) for devices, CLIs and AI/MCP clients without a browser. Off unless enabled. The person enters the user code on a page this server renders (the host may supply its own page markup), then signs in and approves through the host's interaction route, where the host applies step-up; PendingInteraction.deviceFlow says which flow it is. user-code-charset: base-20 (consonants without look-alikes) or digits. user-code-mask: * stands for one character. throttle: wrong user codes allowed per client IP within the window before the page answers 429; in process memory, so per instance. The device code lives ttl.device-code seconds. How long the resulting grant lasts is ttl.grant and ttl.refresh-token.
_comment_resource_servers: APIs that accept this server's access tokens, keyed by resource indicator (RFC 8707). A token for a resource names it as its audience, so one API cannot replay another's token. scope: the scopes that API accepts, space-separated. access-token-format: opaque or jwt. access-token-ttl: seconds, defaults to ttl.access-token. A request for a resource not listed here is refused. A token with no resource is good only at UserInfo. A map: a host adds an API without restating the others.
_comment_ttl: Lifetimes in seconds. Session matches ngdpbase's 24-hour session max-age. Grant and refresh token bound how long a client keeps access without the person signing in again.
_comment_audit_events: The audit event registry, keyed by event, in ngdpbase's shape. Names are {target}-{action}. The package reports each event to the host's audit callback; the host's audit manager records it. enabled: whether the event is reported; omitted means true; false is a decision on the record. null removes an entry. on-failure: what happens when the host's callback fails. Only continue is possible here: node-oidc-provider reports an event after the action has happened, so it cannot be refused — a refuse entry stops the boot rather than claim a guarantee nobody keeps. A failed report is counted (auditFailures). Events never carry a token, code or secret. A test holds this map and the code's list equal.

authorization-allow.description: An authorization request succeeded and a code was issued to the client

authorization-deny.description: An authorization request was refused: denied sign-in, unknown resource, bad request

token-issue.description: The token endpoint issued tokens, with the grant type that earned them

token-error.description: The token endpoint refused a request

token-reuse.description: A used authorization code or refresh token was presented again; its grant was revoked

token-revoke.description: An access or refresh token was destroyed, by revocation or with its grant

grant-revoke.description: A grant and every token issued under it were revoked

userinfo-error.description: UserInfo refused a request: invalid, expired or revoked token, unknown account

server-error.description: The server failed while handling a request

_comment_secret_keys: Keys never displayed by a host's configuration screen. Both are environment-only.
_comment_env_keys: Keys owned by the environment, and the variable that supplies each. A key listed here is read only from its variable: setting it in a config file refuses the boot, so a secret cannot end up in one. jwks is a JSON Web Key Set as JSON; cookie-keys is comma-separated.
